A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mamba-HoME and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G. The reordered material in v2 can be matched reliably to v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and PDAC-detection results, cross-modal evaluations, ablations, and qualitative comparisons in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results across CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets, including benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The specified block removes the post-HoME linear projection present in v1 Equation 10 and Figure 1(a); it is absent from v2 Equation 13 and Figure 1(b). The hierarchical routing, Mamba backbone, normalization, and encoder-decoder design remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining datasets and PANORAMA, AMOS, FeTA, MVSeg, and in-house evaluation data. The CT-only, MRI-only, CT-to-MRI, and joint-training scenarios are retained. Expanded acquisition descriptions do not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged after matching main-text and appendix experiments. The VoCo-B row appearing in v2 Table 4 already occurs in the MVSeg comparison in v1 Table 14, so it redisplays an existing comparator.

E3.justification: The group-size ablation's reported fixed experts change from [16,32,48,64] in v1 Appendix E.2 to E1=[4,8,12,16] and E2=[8,16,24,32] in v2 Appendix D.2. Table 6 also revises its exceptional expert configuration. The DyT timing footnote replaces uniform 128×128×128 patches with dataset-specific Appendix B settings. These reported revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Table 8 removes the MVSeg comparison between LayerNorm and DyT, slightly reducing the normalization-ablation evidence. The expert-count, group-size, slot-count, pretraining, HoME-component, and generalizability analyses are otherwise retained after matching the reordered appendices.

E5.justification: AMOS captions no longer describe results as aggregated 'across all folds,' for example v1 Table 12 versus v2 Table 23. FeTA's five-fold protocol, the ± summaries, and the Wilcoxon p<0.05 reporting remain. This changes statistical documentation without establishing changed run counts.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and appendix segmentation/detection scores are retained apart from equivalent rounding. Reported resource figures change: Table 1 revises Mamba-HoME from 170.5M parameters and 11.3G GPU memory to 170.1M and 11.1G, with further revisions in Tables 5–6. Table 8 removes MVSeg's 84.9% and 85.0% normalization-ablation results.

T1.justification: v2 acknowledges that grouped assignment retains total complexity O(N_i M_i d), correcting v1's argument that grouping reduces computational complexity. Reconstruction indexing is also repaired from a slot-indexed output to K_i tokens per group with padding removed, comparing v1 Equation 9 with v2 Equation 11.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the assertion of sparse routing, and the introduction moderates the efficiency claim from unprecedented to competitive. The three central contributions and the claims concerning segmentation performance and cross-modal generalization remain.

C2.justification: The grouping explanation now attributes efficiency benefits to locality and reduced peak memory while acknowledging unchanged total routing complexity. Cross-modal-transfer interpretations and the limitations concerning larger datasets and self-supervised pretraining remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete code-repository address, explicitly reports 32-bit training precision, and expands acquisition statistics and flatten/reshape documentation. v1 already stated that code was provided. Existing hardware, software, optimizer, preprocessing, and training-time details are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual citations, including xLSTM, hierarchical biomedical representations, and TotalSegmentator CT. These broaden background support while retaining the same positioning around integrating Mamba with hierarchical soft expert routing.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially reorganized through new preliminaries and notation, rewritten architecture explanations, and more consistent terminology. Implementation details move into a dedicated main-text subsection, and the appendices gain a contents page and a revised ordering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, qualitative figures are rerendered or cropped, and Figure 3 replaces its middle example. Table 2 becomes full-width, Tables 5–8 receive revised structures, and numerous appendix displays are resized and relocated. This is a broad presentation revision that largely reuses existing evidence.

improvement.justification: The corrected complexity argument, clearer block and ablation specifications, and concrete code address provide a limited overall gain in clarity and reproducibility while retaining the quantitative evidence. The gain is tempered by an apparent labeling inconsistency: Figure 3's replacement MRI-labeled middle example appears to reuse an example shown as AMOS-CT in Figure 6.
